newsitem.title: JAPAN: Recovery in Japan capital spending to continue - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Recovery in Japan capital spending to continue - BOJ.

text.p: Japan's capital spending is likely to keep recovering for the time being, backed by progress in industrial restructuring, the Bank of Japan (BOJ) said in a report released on Wednesday.

In the report on capital spending, the central bank said structural adjustment had reached a point where it was no longer holding back economic recovery and added that it was a factor behind the recent recovery in capital spending.
Recent data showing a firmer economy also suggested capital spending would continue to recover, the report said.
"Taking into account recent leading indicators showing economic firmness, such as machinery orders, capital spending is likely to stick to a recovery path," the BOJ said in the report.
It said the recovery in capital spending had started to become more solid recently and was spreading to various sectors of the economy.

It said the cycle of low interest rates and fiscal measures, coupled with restructuring efforts leading to higher profits at major firms and then to other firms, was behind the recovery in capital spending.
But the BOJ added that for the recovery in capital spending and the economy as a whole to continue, balance sheets of firms needed to be improved and deregulation pushed forward.
An increase in land transactions would help improve the balance sheet problem, it said.
